newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican exports seen growing 15 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexican exports seen growing 15 pct in 1997.

text.p: Mexican exports will grow by about 15 percent in 1997, said Gilberto Marin Quintero, the president of the National Foreign Trade Council (Conacex)
Speaking at the IV National Congress on Foreign Trade, Marin Quintero told reporters that "next year, there will be growth ... of around 15 percent."

Marin Quintero said official statistics likely will show a growth in 1996 exports of close to 20 percent following export growth in 1995 of 30 percent. The export growth figures were skewed by the December 1994 peso devaluation.
From January to September of this year, exports totalled $69.8 billion meaning exports for the year could reach $100 billion, he said.
Marin Quintero said the current exchange rate of nearly eight pesos to the dollar is "a competitive exchange rate."

"We don't think the exchange rate is the only factor behind the growth in exports," he said, accompanied by presidents of two other foreign trade associations. "It's a factor that helps, but it's not fundamental. Productivity is fundamental."
